newsitem.title: UK: Inchcape slips after H1 in weaker market.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape slips after H1 in weaker market.

text.p: Shares in Inchcape Plc fell on Monday after reporting flat pre-tax profits for the first half, but traders said the drop reflected a cautious mark-down in a weaker stock market rather than disappointment over the figures.
The shares moved 9-1/2p lower to 293p in late morning after reporting profits of 82.8 million stg to June 30, little changed from last year's 83.3 million stg.
Analysts had forecast profits of between 73 to 88 million stg.
"The shares are fairly steady now. Volumes are very low today and it's no more than a cautious markdown," said a trader.
"Our analyst was positive in front of the meeting and I don't think he changed his mind after it," he said.
Another analyst said there was nothing untoward that had emerged from the meeting to warrant share price weakness.

Inchcape said the interim payout for the first half of 4.2 pence per share compared with six pence last year was in line with a more conventional approach now being taken by the group to pay a smaller interim dividend and seek to make the final dividend larger.
